course_position.stage_name: Toward B1 - Complex Conversations and Narratives

lesson_intent.one_sentence_goal: Practice identifying a specific object with a short som clause.
lesson_intent.real_life_context: A small workplace problem involving a lost or found item.
lesson_intent.communicative_function: Clarifying exactly which object or place is being discussed.

dialogue_task.scenario: Anna and Erik try to figure out whether a found umbrella, jacket, or bag belongs to someone nearby.

main_focus.name: som clauses after object nouns
main_focus.description: Use som after an object noun to specify the item without overexplaining.
model_examples: Är det väskan som låg vid dörren?
Jag letar efter paraplyet som jag hade i morse.
main_focus.desired_presence: Use object-focused som clauses naturally 2-3 times.

useful_chunks: Är det den som låg här?
Jag tror att den tillhör någon annan.
Vad skönt att den kom fram.
vocabulary_target.desired_presence: Use practical object and location words that make the small problem easy to follow.

dialogue_shape.opening: One speaker notices or asks about a missing item.
dialogue_shape.middle: They describe the item and where it was using som clauses.
dialogue_shape.ending: They solve the small problem or decide what to do with the item.

target_complexity.repetition: repeat the target pattern with two different objects if natural

focus: the small problem in the conversation
which item is being identified and how
the outcome or next step for the item

sentence_focus: one sentence with som describing a lost item
one sentence about where something was
one sentence asking if an object belongs to someone
one sentence giving the outcome of the small problem
